items.summary:
Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character vulnerability in the AdoNetAppender of Apache log4net.

Text parameters were bound unchanged, so a NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate reached the database as it was. A database that refuses such a value, such as PostgreSQL, rejected the insert and the event was lost; only the first such loss per appender was reported. A party whose data reaches a log message could suppress that event.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.
items.title: Apache log4net: AdoNetAppender loses an event whose text the database cannot store

items.summary:
Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the FileAppender, RollingFileAppender, UdpAppender and SmtpAppender of Apache log4net.

Characters the configured encoding could not represent were converted by that encoding's best-fit fallback, which turns fullwidth characters such as U+FF1C, U+FF1E and U+FF02 into <, > and ". The conversion happened after XmlLayout or XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J had escaped the text, so a party whose data reaches a log message could forge complete log events in an XML log, for example a fake audit entry. On .NET Framework this needs no configuration where the ANSI code page is single-byte, since that is the default encoding; on .NET it needs a configured single-byte encoding such as ISO-8859-1. This is the best-fit conversion described by the WorstFit research.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.
items.title: Apache log4net: Best-fit encoding in FileAppender lets fullwidth text forge XML log events

items.summary:
Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J of Apache log4net.

Both layouts split a message holding the CDATA end marker into several CDATA sections, but searched for the marker with a culture-sensitive comparison. Ignorable characters or a combining mark around the marker made the search miss it, so the CDATA section stayed open. From 3.3.1 on, an XML parser then reads the following log events as part of that message; earlier versions leave the log file not well-formed. A party whose data reaches a log message could hide later log events from a consumer that parses the XML log.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.
items.title: Apache log4net: Culture-sensitive CDATA end search in XmlLayout hides later log events

items.summary: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.8.7, web/html/socio/sistema/processa_edicao_socio.php updates member information without validating an authenticated session. An unauthenticated remote requester who supplies a target member identifier and replacement member fields can modify arbitrary member records, corrupt personal information, and cause loss of data integrity. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.7.
items.title: WeGIA: Missing Authentication in processa_edicao_socio.php Allows Unauthorized Member Data Modification

items.summary: WeGIA is a web manager for charitable institutions. Prior to 3.9.1, web/controle/control.php authorizes FuncionarioControle requests only by checking whether an authenticated employee has a permission row for resource 11 or 91, while MiddlewareDAO::verificarPermissao() does not compare the stored id_acao value or authorize the requested method. An employee with any such permission and a valid CSRF token from the employee's own session can invoke FuncionarioControle::adicionarPermissao, FuncionarioControle::alterarPermissao, or FuncionarioControle::excluirPermissao to add, change, or remove permissions for arbitrary roles. This can grant higher action levels over sensitive resources, expose or modify protected employee, patient, configuration, and administrative data, or disrupt legitimate access by changing other roles. This issue is fixed in version 3.9.1.
items.title: WeGIA: Authenticated Privilege Escalation due to Missing Action-level Authorisation

items.summary: Servo is a lightweight, high-performance web rendering engine for embedding web technologies in applications. Prior to 0.4.0, a frame with sandbox="" can reach and execute a javascript: URL through declarative refresh because RefreshRedirectDue::invoke() in components/script/dom/document/document.rs can reach JavaScript URL handling in components/script/script_thread.rs without enforcing the sandbox's script prohibition. This gives attacker-controlled content arbitrary JavaScript execution in a frame intended to be scriptless, including nested DOM probe creation and blind browser requests. The frame retains an opaque origin, so the issue does not by itself provide parent DOM access. This issue is fixed in version 0.4.0.
items.title: Servo Sandbox bypass: `meta refresh` can execute `javascript:` in `sandbox=""`

items.summary: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. From 0.29.0 to 0.40.2, Atomic Server provisions a well-known /setup invite with write enabled, the Drive root as its target, and usagesLeft set to one. construct_invite_redirect in server/src/plugins/invite.rs discards the redeemer identity, so an unauthenticated request containing an attacker-controlled public-key can create a new Agent and grant it write access to the entire Drive. On a fresh, unclaimed deployment, this permits reading, modifying, or deleting resources, changing permissions, and creating or altering Agents. No complete fixed version was verified as of this review.
items.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated `/setup` invite grants write access to the entire Drive

items.summary: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. Prior to 6.7, log_http_access in src/webserver/webserver.c writes attacker-controlled User-Agent content to the access log without output neutralization when debug.api is enabled. If an administrator configures files.log.webserver inside webserver.paths.webroot with a filename matching lua_server_page_pattern, an unauthenticated request can plant Lua markup in that log and a later request can cause CivetWeb to evaluate the log as a Lua server page. The resulting commands run as the pihole operating-system user and can access or modify pihole-owned configuration, credentials, databases, logs, and rendered interface content. When the log is not served through the Lua handler, the same unneutralized writer still permits log forgery and downstream log-parser injection. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.
items.title: Pi-hole FTL: Log injection in webserver access-log writer chains to remote code execution via Lua-server-page evaluation

items.summary: Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.0 until 6.7, validation in src/api/list.c permits spaces for GRAVITY_GROUPS and consequently skips carriage-return and line-feed validation for group names submitted through POST /api/groups. The unsanitized name is copied into the Location value in pi_hole_extra_headers, and CivetWeb interprets embedded CR/LF sequences as separate HTTP response headers. An authenticated administrator can therefore inject headers such as Set-Cookie, Location, or Cache-Control; when a browser processes the response, this can cause session fixation, attacker-controlled redirects, or cache behavior changes. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.
items.title: Pi-hole FTL: CRLF Injection / HTTP Header Injection via Group Name

items.summary: wishthis through 1.2.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in User::ownsWishlist() that allows authenticated users to modify other users' wishes and wishlists. Attackers can supply sequential wish_id and wishlist_id values to the wishes and wishlists API handlers to edit wishes, add wishes, or rename and delete wishlists.
items.title: wishthis through 1.2.3 Authorization Bypass via ownsWishlist Ownership Check

items.summary: Bonsai through 6.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editor users to access admin pages because AdminAuthHandler accepts both Administrator and Editor roles. Attackers can use UsersController and DynamicConfigController to reset administrator passwords, promote accounts to Administrator, and change global settings to take over the instance.
items.title: Bonsai through 6.0 Incorrect Authorization in Admin Users and Config Controllers

items.summary: Habitat through 1.7.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in CreatePostController::addAttachmentsToPost() that allows authenticated users to claim other users' unposted image uploads. Email-verified attackers can submit sequential attachmentIds when creating a post to attach another user's pending image, exposing it publicly and removing it from the uploader's post.
items.title: Habitat through 1.7.1 IDOR via Post Creation Attachment IDs

items.summary: ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the IAM role management API that allows authenticated tenant members to escalate privileges. Attackers holding even the lowest built-in role can call the permissions/grant-ids, permissions/grant, or bind/member routes to grant permissions or bind privileged roles, gaining tenant administrative access.
items.title: ArtisanCloud PowerX through 1.0.2 Privilege Escalation via IAM Role Endpoints

items.summary: linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by passing unvalidated redirectUri values on the Login and Logout pages. Attackers can craft login links sending victims to attacker-controlled sites after authentication, and inject persistent returnTo destinations into other users' logout redirects via the shared AuthInformation instance.
items.title: linkdotnet Blog through 17.1 Open Redirect via redirectUri Parameter

items.summary: tac_plus-ng before commit d8493e0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows clients holding the TACACS+ shared key to overflow a stack buffer due to an operator precedence error in author_pak_looks_bogus() and accounting_pak_looks_bogus(). Attackers can send packets whose argument-length table exceeds the payload, causing eval_args() to read past the packet and memcpy() oversized cmd values into cmdline, crashing the daemon or executing code.
items.title: tac_plus-ng before commit d8493e0 Stack-Based Buffer Overflow via packet length checks

items.summary: Kiwi TCMS is an open source test management system. From 16.1 until 16.2, the account confirmation page’s incomplete validation of the next parameter accepts protocol-relative URLs because the version 16.1 fix for CVE-2026-54724 only requires the value to start with a slash. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a confirmation URL on a trusted Kiwi TCMS hostname that redirects a user to an external site, enabling phishing and related downstream confidentiality or integrity impacts when the user follows the link. This issue is fixed in version 16.2.
items.title: Kiwi TCMS : Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54724: open redirect bypass via protocol-relative URL in account confirmation

items.summary: Mistune is a Python Markdown parser with renderers and plugins. Prior to 3.3.4, inline image parsing sends nested ![ openers through precedence_scan because the no_link_before and _label_contains_link linearization guards are gated by not is_image. In src/mistune/inline_parser.py, each outer image opener can therefore search the remaining image body, while max_image_depth does not apply because the failed scans do not produce image tokens. Rendering untrusted Markdown with the default HTML renderer and no plugins can perform quadratic CPU work and keep a worker at 100 percent utilization. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.4.
items.title: Mistune: Quadratic-time DoS in inline image parsing (precedence_scan) bypasses not-is-image guards

items.summary: matrix-hookshot is a Matrix bot for connecting to external services like GitHub, GitLab, JIRA, and more. Prior to 7.3.3, Hookshot can crash in src/Bridge.ts while processing a modern Matrix reply whose m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to.event_id identifies an event that the bot cannot read. Bridge event handling calls botClient.getEvent() for the parent event without catching the resulting M_NOT_FOUND error, allowing the rejected request to escape reply processing and terminate the service. This issue is fixed in version 7.3.3.
items.title: matrix-hookshot: Denial of service by replying to an event Hookshot can not read

items.summary: code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can call the autocomplete API with a request endpoint that contains the configured remote endpoint only as a substring. The endpoint validation uses an unanchored regular expression, so a different internal route can satisfy the check and be invoked server-side through the autocomplete request. The vulnerable path uses SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteEndpoint(); applications using SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteCallback() are not affected by this endpoint-selection flaw. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.
items.title: code16/sharp: Server-side request forgery through an unanchored autocomplete endpoint check

items.summary: Phoenix is an AI observability and evaluation platform. From 13.0.0 until 15.7.0, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passed attacker-controlled F-string templates to FStringTemplateFormatter._format, while DotDict.__getattr__ did not prevent traversal through Python private attributes. A crafted field could traverse object internals such as __class__, __init__, and __globals__ to read process environment variables and internal module state. The endpoint is unauthenticated on default installations, and any account can reach it when authentication is enabled. Exposure of PHOENIX_SECRET can allow administrative session-token forgery and decryption of credentials protected by keys derived from that secret. This issue is fixed in version 15.7.0.
items.title: Phoenix: Format String Injection in applyChatTemplate

items.summary: A vulnerability was found in sergix44 XBackBone up to 3.8.2. Impacted is the function MediaController::getRawById of the file app/Controllers/MediaController.php. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.
items.title: sergix44 XBackBone MediaController.php getRawById cross site scripting

items.summary: A security vulnerability has been detected in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This vulnerability affects the function fs.readFileSync of the file local.provider.ts of the component Custom Page Handler. The manipulation of the argument path leads to path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version test-20261013 is able to resolve this issue. The identifier of the patch is d63aa163f10b6dc1080e2368fe8e71aa95b765cb. Upgrading the affected component is advised.
items.title: Mereithhh VanBlog Custom local.provider.ts fs.readFileSync path traversal

items.summary: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, when the pipelined request queue is full, the pure-Python parser stores the unparsed remainder internally and also returns the same data to its caller. After a handler declines an upgrade request, the caller feeds the remainder back to the parser, causing the buffer to grow with each handled request and dispatching already-handled requests to the application again. The issue affects deployments using AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS or otherwise running without the standard C-extension wheel, and can cause excessive memory use and repeated request processing. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.
items.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request replay and buffer growth behind a declined upgrade

items.summary: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, Request.post() does not limit the number of fields in a URL-encoded form body, and inserting many repeated keys into MultiDict takes quadratic time on the event loop. A remote attacker can send a form POST within client_max_size to a handler that calls Request.post() and block the event loop. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.
items.title: AIOHTTP: Too many URL-encoded form fields block the event loop

items.summary: SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. From version 4.7.0 until versions 7.2.10 and 8.0.2, @sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare allowed an attacker-influenced link crawled during prerendering to place whitespace, control characters, wildcards, or placeholders into a prerendered redirect path. The adapter wrote those paths into the Cloudflare _redirects output without output-context validation, allowing a path to create unintended routing rules that could redirect or expose requests beyond the intended prerendered route. This issue is fixed in 7.2.10 and 8.0.2.
items.title: SvelteKit: Prerendered redirect paths can inject arbitrary rules into the `_redirects` file generated by `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare`

items.summary: SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. From version 3.0.0 until 3.1.1, the build-time server-only module guard did not treat src/params.js as a client entry point even though parameter matchers can run in the browser. Server-only modules imported through src/params.js could consequently enter the client bundle, where statically replaced private environment values or other server secrets could be exposed. This issue is fixed in 3.1.1.
items.title: SvelteKit: Build-time server-only module import guard could fail, resulting in server secrets being statically replaced in client bundle

items.summary: dnspython is a DNS toolkit for Python. Prior to version 2.9.2, the from_text() parser for WKS records does not require the service number to be between 0 and 65535 before using it as a bitmap offset. An attacker-controlled zone file can supply a larger number, causing the service bitmap to grow to an extremely large size through inefficient repeated extension, consuming excessive memory and CPU and potentially terminating the process. Applications are affected only when they parse zone-file text whose record type and rdata are attacker controlled. This issue is fixed in version 2.9.2.
items.title: dnspython excessive memory and CPU use

items.summary: Hubleys is a dashboard for self-hosted services. Prior to version 0.5.2, any authenticated (non-admin) Hubleys user can upload a file with an arbitrary extension as their dashboard "background image," and the server will later serve that file back with a Content-Type derived straight from the attacker's chosen extension - so uploading an .html file gets it served as text/html. Because the endpoint that serves it returns a manually-constructed response rather than going through SvelteKit's normal page-rendering pipeline, the app's configured Content-Security-Policy never gets attached to it either, so a script embedded in the upload runs unrestricted. This issue has been patched in version 0.5.2.
items.title: Hubleys: Stored XSS via unrestricted background-image upload, served with an attacker-chosen Content-Type and no CSP protection

items.summary: OpenTelemetry-Go is the Go implementation of OpenTelemetry. From SDK version 1.33.0, SDK log version 0.9.0, and trace version 1.35.0 until version 1.47.0, the AttributeValueLengthLimit and WithAttributeValueLengthLimit truncation paths in sdk/internal/attrnorm, sdk/log/internal/attrnorm, and trace/auto.go do not count valid U+FFFD replacement characters. This is a distinct incomplete-fix defect in the replacement truncation code introduced by the remediation for CVE-2026-81869. Values composed of or dominated by those characters can therefore exceed the configured character and memory bound in span, log-record, and auto-instrumentation trace attributes. Attacker-controlled telemetry attributes can increase retained memory and pipeline pressure, while confidentiality and integrity are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.47.0.
items.title: opentelemetry-go: AttributeValueLengthLimit is fully bypassed by attribute values composed of valid U+FFFD runes

items.summary: Laravel is a web application framework. Prior to 12.71.0 and 13.40.0, Laravel's Concurrency::run process driver can treat a forged internal result message in child standard output as framework output. An application route must invoke Concurrency::run, and a task must write attacker-controlled bytes at the start of the child's standard output that form a complete JSON document followed by gzip magic bytes. Under those application-specific conditions, an attacker can forge the internal result message and achieve remote code execution. The affected behavior is not exposed by default and requires application code that routes untrusted input into task output. This issue is fixed in versions 12.71.0 and 13.40.0.
items.title: Laravel: Task Output Injection - Concurrency Process

items.summary: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, the BACnet/SC hub's Linux WebSocket server reassembles fragmented WebSocket messages into a per-connection fragment_buffer. It grows that buffer with realloc() on every non-final frame, with no upper bound. A peer that streams binary continuation fragments and never sets FIN keeps the hub reallocating until the box runs out of memory or the process is OOM-killed. The buffer starts at the maximum legal BVLC-SC NPDU size, but nothing after that ties its growth back to that limit. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.
items.title: BACnet Stack: BACnet/SC hub grows its WebSocket reassembly buffer without limit, so a peer can exhaust its memory

items.summary: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE implementation accepts AtomicWriteFile(record-access) requests that replace existing records with caller-controlled content. If a client replaces a record with shorter data, the backend can shrink the heap allocation and then continue processing with a trailing-copy length derived from the old layout. During that replace path, the RAMFS backend computes the trailing-copy length from the old file layout, then shrinks the heap allocation, and finally uses the stale length in memmove(). As a result, the source range of that memmove() can extend beyond the end of the reallocated heap buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.
items.title: BACnet Stack: Replacing a RAMFS record with a shorter one via `AtomicWriteFile(record-access)` can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read

items.summary: envd provides reproducible development environments for humans and agents. In versions starting with 0.3.38 and before 1.3.6, insufficient containment of host-side requirements-file reads in  install.python_packages(requirements=...)  could allow access to files outside the build context. An attacker able to influence build input could cause file contents interpreted as dependency entries to appear in debug logs or build-step metadata, subject to the envd process’s permissions. Exploitation in version 1.3.5 additionally requires concurrent modification of relevant filesystem paths. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.6.
items.title: envd: Host file disclosure through requirements path traversal and TOCTOU

items.summary: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From 3.21.6 to before 4.0.0 and from 4.4.6 until 4.6.4, the /__nuxt_island path hash uses ohash serialization that does not escape quotes in string values or delimiters in object keys, allowing different island-prop tuples to produce the same path. For prerendering, substituted content is written into the generated page only if the crawler reaches a colliding URL before rendering the page with the legitimate props. Separately, a CDN or reverse proxy that keys island responses by path alone can be primed with the colliding response. If the substituted prop reaches v-html, innerHTML, or another unsafe HTML sink, the response can execute script in the application origin; otherwise the impact is content substitution. Applications that do not use server components or NuxtIsland, islands without attacker-influenced string props, and responses not cached by path alone are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
items.title: Nuxt: Colliding island props can share one `/__nuxt_island` path (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-46342)

items.summary: Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. Nuxt from 3.0.0 until 4.6.4, @nuxt/nitro-server from 3.20.0 until 4.6.4, and @nuxt/vite-server from 4.6.0 until 4.6.4, routeRules matching leaves an encoded slash (%2F) in the request path while a catch-all page such as app/pages/[...slug].vue or a custom multi-segment page route decodes it into a route parameter. The getRouteRules result is therefore incomplete, and an unauthenticated request can render the page without the redirect, headers, proxy, SSR, noScripts, appMiddleware, or appLayout rules configured for the decoded path. Protected content is resolved only when the page interprets the decoded parameter accordingly: a custom multi-segment parameter can contain the decoded path, while a repeatable catch-all must join the slash-containing array element; route.path remains encoded and does not resolve that resource. Static pages, single-segment parameters, server/api handlers, and server/routes handlers are not affected because they do not have the same encoded-path mismatch. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.
items.title: Nuxt: Incomplete fix for GHSA-6gq8-jgmh-3ffp: an encoded slash (`%2F`) in the request path bypasses route rules on catch-all page routes

items.summary: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a malformed but non-empty BACnet WriteProperty request can drive the official server demo into a non-terminating request-processing loop with repeated heap-backed side effects. This results in a remote unauthenticated denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption and a non-terminating request path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
items.title: BACnet Stack: Remote unauthenticated DoS in `Life_Safety_Zone` `PROP_ZONE_MEMBERS` WriteProperty parsing

items.summary: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a BACnet/SC peer can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read (up to 3 bytes), pre-authentication, in the BACnet/SC header-option decoder. bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option() reads the vendor-id and option-type at fixed offsets [3],[4],[5] before checking the option's declared header length, and the option-list validator never enforces a minimum length for proprietary options. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.
items.title: BACnet Stack: Out-of-bounds read in BACnet/SC proprietary header-option decode (bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option)

items.summary: BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2, a reachable out-of-bounds write exists when encoding the device.address-binding property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2.
items.title: BACnet Stack: Global APDU transmit buffer out-of-bounds write in device.address-binding response encoding via address_list_encode()

items.summary: Zipline before 4.6.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in GET /api/server/folder/:id that allows unauthenticated attackers to list files in non-public upload-only folders. Attackers who know the folder UUID can supply the page query parameter to bypass the metadata-only early return and enumerate file names, IDs, MIME types, sizes, and view counts.
items.title: Zipline before 4.6.4 Unauthenticated File Listing via page Query Parameter

items.summary: Zipline from 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that logs sensitive environment variable values, such as OAUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, without redaction at startup. Attackers with access to system journal or docker logs can obtain OAuth2 client secrets and use them to exchange intercepted OAuth2 callbacks for valid tokens.
items.title: Zipline 4.2.0 before 4.6.2 OAuth2 Client Secret Leakage in Startup Logs

items.summary: Zipline through 4.4.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the PATCH /api/user/files/:id rename endpoint that allows authenticated users to overwrite existing uploads by supplying unsanitized names. Attackers can submit names like ../uploads/victim.txt that bypass the raw-string database uniqueness check but normalize via path.join(), causing fs.rename() to replace other files' contents.
items.title: Zipline through 4.4.0 Path Traversal File Overwrite via PATCH /api/user/files/:id

items.summary: Huginn before 2026.11.09 contains an information exposure vulnerability in JqAgent that allows authenticated users to read the server process environment because the jq child process inherits it. Attackers who can create, configure or dry-run a JqAgent can supply a filter using env or $ENV to disclose APP_SECRET_TOKEN, database, SMTP and OAuth secrets.
items.title: Huginn before 2026.11.09 Information Exposure via JqAgent jq env Builtin

items.summary: Ryot before 10.5.6 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to take over other users' collections by supplying an updateId to the createOrUpdateCollection GraphQL mutation. Attackers who know a collection id can trigger ownership reassignment without checks, read its items, rewrite metadata, and evict the original owner and collaborators.
items.title: Ryot before 10.5.6 Authorization Bypass via createOrUpdateCollection updateId

items.summary: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, contain an improper path equivalence flaw in VirtualFileFactory.canonicalisePath that bypasses mount-level access policy. Authenticated users can supply paths with duplicate separators or dot segments to route operations to a less restrictive parent mount and read or write files the child mount denies.
items.title: Jadaptive Maverick Synergy Server before 3.0.33 and 3.1.x before 3.1.7, and Maverick Legacy Server before 1.8.1, VFS Mount Policy Bypass via Non-Canonical Paths

items.summary: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability because Mage_Api_Model_Session::_renewBySessId() never checks api_user.is_active and REST OAuth authorization never checks whether the admin user is active. Attackers holding an existing SOAP/XML-RPC session or OAuth access token retain API access after deactivation or API key rotation, reading and modifying customer, order and catalog data.
items.title: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 Insufficient Session Expiration After API User Deactivation

items.summary:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively you could use a build of Axis with the patch from https://github.com/apache/axis-axis1-java/commit/41f3b4e8d04e310ca81f86b92630ab2c11d608bd applied. The Apache Axis project does not expect to create an Axis 1.x release fixing this problem.
items.title: Apache Axis 1.x (EOL): unauthenticated remote class instantiation via SOAP fault exceptionName

items.summary: Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 contains a configuration injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with IPsec Mobile privileges to execute commands as root via the login_banner field. Attackers can submit a single-line banner containing '}' to escape the unquoted strongswan.conf attr value and define charon.start-scripts entries that charon executes as root on restart.
items.title: Netgate pfSense CE 2.7.0 through 2.9.0 and Plus through 26.07 Command Injection via IPsec Mobile Login Banner

items.summary: A flaw was found in CRI-O's `bind_mount_prefix` handling. When configured with a non-empty `bind_mount_prefix`, a malicious container or local attacker could use a Container Runtime Interface (CRI) hostPath containing an intermediate absolute symlink. This could cause the bind mount source to resolve outside the intended prefixed root, potentially leading to unauthorized access to files or privilege escalation on the host system.
items.title: Cri-o: cri-o: bind_mount_prefix intermediate-symlink prefix bypass

items.summary: Twig versions 2.16.x and 3.9.0 through 3.25.x contain a sandbox bypass vulnerability when using a SourcePolicyInterface that allows attackers with template rendering capabilities to pass arbitrary PHP callables to sort, filter, map, and reduce filters.
